test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1) Foundational Full Test - 02
subject: general
question: A table and a swing were sold for Rs. 9,936 each. The table was sold for a profit of 8% and the swing was sold for a loss of 8%. What is the gain or loss percentage in the whole transaction?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When two articles are sold at the exact same selling price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, the entire transaction always results in an overall loss.

Overall Loss % = (x² ÷ 100)%

⇒ Overall Loss % = (8² ÷ 100)% = (64 ÷ 100)% = 0.64%

**∴ The correct answer is 0.64% loss.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of the table = ₹9936

Selling Price (SP) of the swing = ₹9936

Profit on the table = 8%

Loss on the swing = 8%

 
 CP1 = 9200
 
 

 Profit = +8% (+736)

 
 SP1 = 9936

 
 CP2 = 10800
 
 

 Loss = −8% (−864)

 
 SP2 = 9936
 
 Total CP = 20000 | Total SP = 19872 | Loss = 128
 Overall Loss % = (128 ÷ 20000) × 100 = 0.64%

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Selling Price = 9936 + 9936 = ₹19872

⇒ Cost Price of the table (CP₁) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]

⇒ CP₁ = 9936 × (100 ÷ 108) = 9936 × (25 ÷ 27) = ₹9200

⇒ Cost Price of the swing (CP₂) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)]

⇒ CP₂ = 9936 × (100 ÷ 92) = 9936 × (25 ÷ 23) = ₹10800

⇒ Total Cost Price = 9200 + 10800 = ₹20000

⇒ Total Loss = Total CP − Total SP = 20000 − 19872 = ₹128

⇒ Overall Loss % = (Total Loss ÷ Total CP) × 100

⇒ Overall Loss % = (128 ÷ 20000) × 100 = 0.64%

**∴ The correct answer is 0.64% loss.**

**__Additional Information__**

Same SP, Same Profit & Loss %

When two items are sold at the same selling price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always a net loss. The loss percentage is consistently determined using the formula (x² ÷ 100)%.

Same CP, Same Profit & Loss %

When two items are bought at the identical cost price, and one is sold at a profit of x% while the other at a loss of x%, the net result is zero, meaning there is no net profit and no net loss overall.

Marked Price and CP Relation

The direct ratio comparing Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP) when dealing with profit and discount is written directly as: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
